caseStudyContent.heading: Mavenoid’s Product Support Community serves as a global hub for technical support leaders

body: Support leaders at hardware and electronics companies face tough, unique challenges—and until now, there’s been no dedicated place for them to connect and share real solutions.

Mavenoid’s Product Support Community (PSC) changes that. It’s the first (and only) community built exclusively for technical support leaders, focused on practical takeaways for support teams and the latest advancements in automation and AI.
caseStudyContent.heading: The precision of hardware and the people who power its support.

body: The design system for the Product Support Community (PSC) is deliberately built on two contrasting yet harmonious layers: a grounded “material world” foundation and a vibrant communal overlay that elevates the brand into something more human and connected.

Key results Boosted campaign MQLs by 150% through the strategic design of high-performing community content and social assets. Influenced 22% of marketing-attributed deals by delivering persuasive brand collateral.

At its core, the system begins with the material—bold outlines (inherited directly from the parent Mavenoid brand), and a restrained blue palette that keeps everything feeling corporate, trustworthy, and buttoned-up. This layer is the nuts and bolts: reliable, precise, and unmistakably technical.

The second component to this balance is the communal—or spiritual level, by leaning into bold vector fills to create impact, sometimes offset when the moment calls for it. Rounded corners create a playful-yet-powerful illustration style to soften the edges, making complex technical topics approachable and keeping the community feeling warm rather than coldly corporate. Yellow is introduced intentionally as the spark of connection and energy—used sparingly in accents, highlights, and “pop-out” moments. These bright yellow pop-outs do double duty: they draw the eye to what matters most (like a pop-up notification or chat bubble demanding attention) while symbolizing that community connection.

The nut-and-bolt logo ties it all together: two simple, material forms that only achieve strength when community members come together. Each new member is another turn of the bolt—fitting perfectly, holding stronger, building something unbreakable. The result is a design language that feels simultaneously grounded in the physical world of hardware and lifted by the spiritual warmth of community.
Role: Creative direction, campaign design, illustration, motion design, brand design system

body: Lob is the only direct mail platform with proprietary advanced routing, printing, and delivery infrastructure that delivers predictable postage costs and dramatically faster mail delivery times across the United States.

Built for high-volume teams that send millions of sophisticated, hyper-personalized mailpieces, Lob’s brand is deliberately bold, modern, and distinctive—just like the forward-thinking companies that power their businesses with us.
caseStudyContent.heading: Your direct mail partner from campaign to mailbox

body: Lob’s Template Gallery now has 40+ beautiful, ready-to-use mail pieces (postcards, gift card carriers, snap packs, letters, self-mailers). I scrapped the old, outdated Lob InDesign library for fresh, new templates—clean, modern, and built 100% for the new Figma-to-Lob plugin so customers can customize and send in minutes instead of weeks.
caseStudyContent.heading: Beautiful templates that turn “snail mail” into “sale mail”

body: We built the Lob brand in the same spirit as the platform: to dominate at enterprise scale and never blend in. Fresh, contemporary, and loud—designed to stand beside the most ambitious, design-obsessed companies in the world. Teams sending millions of pieces refuse to let their mail look like junk. So why would they accept a junk-looking mail platform?

Working alongside the Brand Design Manager, I helped evolve the full Lob brand ecosystem: expanding the illustration system, refreshing mail templates, crafting standout event branding, designing physical print collateral, and unifying the promotional visual identity across ads, social media, and the blog. At the heart of the brand is a bright, CMYK-inspired palette that celebrates the essence of print. Indigo always leads—Lob’s bold primary color that refuses to blend in. Together, these colors pop vividly on paper and cut effortlessly through cluttered mailboxes and digital feeds.

GrubClub stems from a passion for entomology and a mission to reframe Western attitudes toward alternative proteins. The project demonstrates that even a deeply stigmatized food source, like eating insects, can spark curiosity and cultural risk-taking when framed the right way through thoughtful design.
caseStudyContent.heading: Delicious meal kits that quietly revolutionize protein

body: GrubClub was born from a love of great food and planet-friendly thinking, we’re on a mission to prove insect protein isn’t weird—it’s wonderful. Every box hides a secret: big, irresistible flavour and powerhouse nutrition, with the bug protein playing the sneakiest hide-and-seek, until you’re fully prepared to uncover the true genius behind the taste.

The circle is GrubClub’s core motif: simple, calm, complete. Scaling seamlessly from the smallest design element to the broadest brand philosophy, it’s in our logo, illustrations, packaging, and every dish. There’s no creepy bug photos—just simple geometry. Everything loops back to one clear message: nature belongs on your plate.
caseStudyContent.heading: Nature, perfectly plated

body: Conceptualized as my senior design thesis, GrubClub puts flavour first and lets the source play hide-and-seek. The brand motif features two-level camouflage: just as the insect protein slips unnoticed into delicious meals, the visual identity does the same. Bold, juicy vector illustrations of vegetables and leaves burst with appetizing colour, creating an instantly mouth-watering, plant-based impression. Blended seamlessly within the foliage are tiny insects, rendered in the same friendly geometric style. They remain perfectly camouflaged until the moment of the joyful double-take.

Underpinning everything is the circle; full circle. It represents nature’s closed loop, a dinner plate, and the simplified anatomy of an insect. These two versatile motifs drive a unique geometric illustration system: minimal and clean on small labels, expanding into bug-hidden scenes across packaging and digital campaigns.
Role: Creative direction, brand design system, motion design, packaging, illustration, campaign creative
caseStudyContent.heading: GrubClub

body: The State of Remote Engineering Report explores the sentiments of software engineers regarding working from home during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic. The report is based on survey data and includes insights from over 1000 engineers from across the world on how economic uncertainties have affected their teams, as well as their opinions on remote work, benefits, the future of work post-pandemic and what companies can offer prospective employees.

The illustration system employed recognizable day-to-day workspaces that engineers often encounter in remote environments while working from home, such as zoom call screens, physical sheets of paper, and the overlapping windows on a desktop. These technical-inspired line illustrations were balanced with abstract pixels that evoke the digital space of the internet - a hub for collaboration and the ideal environment for engineers to do their best work.
Role: Art direction, campaign creative, editorial design, illustration
Creative direction: Mel Lavigne
caseStudyContent.heading: Engineers have a lot to say on remote work and the future of work post-pandemic.

body: House of Balloons (HOB) is a recording studio and creative brand built for producers, engineers, and artists who define their own sound through fearless improvisation. Its visual identity—Arrangement—is a fluid, DAW-inspired system that distills chaos into clarity and process into refined style. At its core is a modular grid designed not to constrain, but to be endlessly pushed to the limit. HOB isn’t for producers who stay on the grid. It’s for the ones who rearrange it.
caseStudyContent.heading: A visual system for producers who break the mold.

body: Directly inspired by the intuitive ways music creators work, Arrangement is the design system for House of Balloons.

Stretch captures the pure digital feel of grabbing a clip in a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) and transforming it on the timeline. It’s that instant, fluid time-bending motion translated into living elasticity: every element in the system can expand, contract, and lock into perfect rhythm, giving the brand a precise yet effortlessly musical breath.

Stack mirrors the modern producer’s workflow of piling tracks vertically in the arrangement view. The brand’s signature grid turns flat musical “bars” into overlapping digital planes that rise and recess with subtle depth and dimension. These layered grids glide and interlock around the typography exactly like tracks in a session, giving letters their own space and velocity.
caseStudyContent.heading: Built around two core conceptual pillars — Stretch and Stack.

body: Producers today are living in a golden age of tools and technology—music production has become a limitless playground for creative expression. Yet with infinite possibilities comes the need for the right frame to shape and focus the sound.

For HOB, I created a new visual identity called Arrangement. Deeply rooted in the modern DAW workflow, improvisation, and the raw creative process, it uses fluid warped typography and a sleek layered grid system as a supportive foundation—one that gives today’s producers and studio artists the perfect frame to shape limitless ideas into focused, powerful sound. The logo features a stylized “o” that serves as a minimalist representation of the balloon at the heart of the studio’s name. More than a simple letterform, it subtly evokes euphoria and heightened states while paying quiet homage to the House of Balloons origin story—The Weeknd’s seminal 2011 debut mixtape.

To scale HOB’s asset production, I built a custom generative motion tool utilizing p5.js. The tool automated the creation of complex motion graphics and looping patterns, delivering ready-to-use reels and video content for social media.
Role: Creative direction, creative concepts, brand guidelines, illustration system, creative coding, motion design
caseStudyContent.heading: Where improvisation becomes identity.

body: Designed to accelerate children’s reading development, Pagemaster connects parents to the perfect local learning program for their kids—no guesswork, no mismatched classes. We understand the real struggle of learning to read, which is why we speak the language of parents and educators alike. One quick skill check on the portal and instantly Pagemaster’s AI engine matches your child to the perfect class, level, and teacher.
caseStudyContent.heading: Pagemaster takes learning beyond the classroom

body: Pagemaster speaks directly to the real struggles kids face when learning to read: intentional spelling mistakes appear in parent-facing materials, a quiet reminder that mistakes are part of the journey. To balance this, ultra-legible Neue Machina with generous ink traps keeps every word clear and effortless for emerging readers. At the heart of the visual system is a bold, expansive black chalkboard paired with clean white typography—the classic classroom canvas. Bright pops of yellow, blue, and coral bring in the joyful energy of real chalk: the same tool teachers use to write lessons and the same toy kids grab to draw hopscotch grids on the sidewalk. It’s a deliberate symbol that learning doesn’t stop at the bell; it spills out into the world.

The strict yet flexible grid system acts as a window to another world—whether that world is reached through the pages of a book, a screen, or the Pagemaster platform itself. Simple rectangles and squares are the most rudimentary shapes, just like learning to read is the first, foundational step toward full literacy. Within the grid lives the secondary logomark: a playful bookworm happily immersed in an open book, welcoming children into deeper stories and adventures.

Hand-drawn accents—scribbled underlines, check marks, and chalky highlights—run throughout the brand. They’re a loving nod to teachers’ pen grades and the satisfying squeak of chalk on a blackboard, but also to the carefree joy of drawing as a child. Every mark says the same thing: learning is serious work and serious play, and it never has to be confined to four walls.
Role: Creative direction, brand design system, illustration, motion design

The Black Friday Cyber Monday (BFCM) By The Numbers Report is an annual data analysis of Shopify merchants’ online sales during the Black Friday shopping season. The report examines how independent businesses have adapted through the pandemic, responded to consumer demand and explored what trends are here to stay.

The line illustration system I created was balanced with geometric translucent charts and arrows. These elements evoke the duality of the global commerce ecosystem, serving as visual metaphors for both the tangible nature of shipped goods and the invisible hand of the market from economic theory.
Role: Illustration, creative concepts, data visualization
